title: Ecommerce return rate statistics for 2026 (+ return fraud)
summary: Ecommerce return rate statistics for 2026: average return rates, return fraud, and holiday returns, sourced from Happy Returns, Wyllo, and Yuma benchmark data.
body_markdown:
In 1875, a Chicago merchant named Aaron Montgomery Ward added a new promise to his mail-order catalog,[a money-back guarantee of customer satisfaction](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Montgomery-Ward) . His customers were farmers buying goods sight unseen from a stranger hundreds of miles away. The promise made the purchase feel safe.


151 years later, ecommerce runs on the same promise. Online shoppers sent back 18% of what they bought in 2026, level with a year earlier, according to Happy Returns'[Returns Happen 2026](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) report. From 2025 to 2026, the rate stayed the same, but pressure grew. Retailers report more concern about return fraud than at any point in the past three years, shoppers expect more from every return, and support teams field the tickets that result.


This report compiles 2026 statistics on return rates, return fees, holiday returns, and return fraud from two Happy Returns studies published this year. It pairs them with production data from 100+ Shopify merchants in Yuma's[2026 CX automation benchmark](https://yuma.ai/cx-automation-benchmark-2026) , which shows what return volume does to a support queue. Along the way, it follows Ward's promise through 150 years of retail, since the numbers read differently once you know where the guarantee came from.


## Ecommerce return rate statistics, the key numbers


Return rates stayed level from 2025 to 2026 in every channel Happy Returns measured. The figures come from its fifth annual study, which surveyed 375 ecommerce professionals at US retailers with $250M or more in revenue and 2,006 consumers who returned an online purchase in the past 12 months.


- **18% of online sales are returned in 2026** , consistent with 2025 ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).
- **15% of total retail sales are returned** , counting online and in-store purchases together ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).
- **9% of in-store sales are returned** , half the online rate ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).


A store shopper can try the jacket on and put it back on the rack before paying. Online shoppers might purposely overbuy to then return what they didn't like.


## How to calculate ecommerce return rate


Divide the number of returned orders (or units) by the total orders (or units) sold during the same timeframe, then multiply by 100.


**Return rate (%) = (returned orders / total orders) x 100**


For example, if a store ships 1,000 orders in a month and customers send back 180 of them, the return rate is (180 / 1,000) x 100 = 18%, which matches the 2026 online average.


Calculate the rate monthly under normal volume and weekly during major sales events. That cadence surfaces a sizing defect on a new SKU, carrier damage on a specific lane, or a spike in policy abuse before the loss reaches a quarterly financial statement.


## Holiday returns and seasonal support peaks


Retailers expect a larger share of holiday sales to come back in 2026 than in either of the two prior seasons. Shoppers plan to send most unwanted gifts back within a month, which pushes the work into January. Yuma's benchmark, built on 12 months of ticket history from June 2025 to May 2026, shows what that calendar looks like from inside a support queue.


- **19% of 2026 holiday sales are expected to come back** , compared with 17% in each of the two prior seasons ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).
- **37% of shoppers plan to return an unwanted gift within a week** , and another 45% within one week to one month ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).
- **40% of merchants hit their busiest support month in Q4** , and 30% in December alone ([Yuma](https://yuma.ai/cx-automation-benchmark-2026) , 2026).
- **17% of merchants peak in Q1** , the months when holiday returns come due, while 25% peak in spring and 14% in summer ([Yuma](https://yuma.ai/cx-automation-benchmark-2026) , 2026).
- **The median merchant's peak month runs 1.5x a normal month** , the busiest quartile reaches 2.2x or higher, and the spikiest brand hit 6x ([Yuma](https://yuma.ai/cx-automation-benchmark-2026) , 2026).


Yuma's peak periods overlap, so the shares add up to more than 100%. Even so, only 40% of merchants hit their busiest month in Q4. A returns plan built only around Black Friday leaves out the other 60%.


## Return fees and the cost of returns in 2026


Retailers are now starting to charge for returns. Charging for at least one return method is now standard practice among large retailers, at an average of about $6. A return fee recovers some of the cost of a return while giving the shopper a reason to keep the item. The recovery still works. The deterrent is fading, as the share of fee-charging retailers that saw return rates fall dropped from 54% in 2024 to 41% in 2026.


- **Return fees average close to $6 where retailers charge them** , from $5.62 to $6.59 depending on the return method ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).
- **41% of retailers that charge fees saw return rates fall** , down from 53% in 2025 and 54% in 2024 ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).
- **50% of retailers that charge fees report more customer complaints** , up from 47% a year earlier ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).
- **39% of retailers that charge fees lost customers** after introducing them ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).
- **58% of retailers call upgrading their returns capabilities an immediate priority** for the next six months ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).


Return fees are reaching their limit. They still recover cost, yet the share of retailers seeing fewer returns because of them dropped 12 points in a year, while half of fee-charging retailers now field more complaints. Fees also create a consistency problem.


A shopper charged $6 by the returns portal and refunded in full by a support agent learns which door to knock on next time. The fraud guides described later in this report are written to find exactly that kind of mismatch. ## Return statistics by channel and method


Box-free drop-off is the most popular return method. The shopper hands the item to staff at a nearby location, with no box or label needed. It also has about one-sixth the fraud rate of mail-in returns, because staff check the item before the refund goes out. A mailed box is opened at the warehouse days later, which gives empty boxes and swapped items a way through.


- **50% of shoppers rank box-free drop-off at a nearby location as their preferred return method** , ahead of the retailer's own store at 27% and returning by mail at 15% ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).
- **Mail-in returns see six times the fraud rate of in-person, box-free drop-offs** ([Happy Returns and Wyllo](https://happyreturns.com/resource/fraud-report-2026) , June 2026).


## Return fraud statistics for 2026


L.L.Bean learned how far a generous guarantee can stretch from a single shirt. The Maine outfitter had backed its products with a satisfaction guarantee for more than a century. Founder Leon Leonwood Bean launched it after 90 of his first 100 pairs of hunting shoes came back. By 2018, some customers were returning L.L.Bean items they had found at thrift stores and yard sales. Shawn Gorman, the founder's great-grandson and the company's chairman,[told the Associated Press](https://komonews.com/news/business/ll-bean-dropping-its-unlimited-returns-policy-02-09-2018-163629377) that a shirt he had donated to Goodwill, with his name printed inside, had been returned to a store. Returns of destroyed or useless items had cost the company $250 million over five years. That February, L.L.Bean replaced its lifetime guarantee with a one-year limit.


The 2026 data shows the same pattern across the whole industry. Retailer concern about return fraud reached a three-year high, even though the fraudulent share of returns stayed level at 8%. Wyllo's consortium data, observed between January 2025 and April 2026, explains why. A small group of repeat offenders causes a disproportionate share of the loss. Wyllo followed one of them for 2.7 years. That person placed 89 orders across 10 retailers, using 25 email addresses and 18 variations of a first name, at a cost of $565,349 in gross merchandise value. Each retailer could see only its own orders.


- **8% of all returns are fraudulent** , excluding policy abuse such as wardrobing, a share that stayed level year over year ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).
- **94% of retailers call return fraud a significant issue** , up from 83% in 2025, with 53% calling it very significant ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).
- **61% of shoppers admit to at least one unethical return behavior** , with 28% admitting to true fraud such as price switching, label tampering, or sending back empty boxes ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).
- **34% of shoppers returned an item with the tags removed in the past year** , 26% returned a worn item, and 19% returned a different item than the one indicated ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).
- **Empty box or box-of-rocks returns are the most prevalent fraud type** , named by 61% of retailers that track fraud ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).
- **Nearly 1 in 5 fraudulent returns comes from organized networks** ([Happy Returns and Wyllo](https://happyreturns.com/resource/fraud-report-2026) , June 2026).
- **1 in 64 orders over $500 involves return fraud** , while 1 in 27 is marked by return policy abuse ([Happy Returns and Wyllo](https://happyreturns.com/resource/fraud-report-2026) , June 2026).
- **About 1% of shoppers are marked as risky returners** , while frequent returners are 85 times more likely to be flagged ([Happy Returns and Wyllo](https://happyreturns.com/resource/fraud-report-2026) , June 2026).
- **80.6% of repeat fraudsters place another fraudulent order within one month** , and 87.0% within two months ([Happy Returns and Wyllo](https://happyreturns.com/resource/fraud-report-2026) , June 2026).
- **A bad actor's average order is $591.87, of which $276.72 is ultimately refunded** ([Happy Returns and Wyllo](https://happyreturns.com/resource/fraud-report-2026) , June 2026).
- **Item verification at drop-off reduces return fraud by at least 85%** compared with mail-in returns ([Happy Returns and Wyllo](https://happyreturns.com/resource/fraud-report-2026) , June 2026).
- **69% of retailers expect return fraud to increase during the holiday season** ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).


The fraud report also describes retailer-specific guides, sold or shared in online fraud communities, that document which customer service escalation paths produce refunds and which agents apply the rules inconsistently. Fraudsters target support teams as well as returns portals. If one agent refuses a refund and another approves the same request, fraudsters learn to keep contacting support until they get a yes. Consistent answers on every ticket remove that opening.

## Return policy and consumer expectation trends


Retailers taught shoppers to expect generous returns. One of the most famous customer service stories in corporate America comes from a Nordstrom store in Fairbanks, Alaska, in the 1970s. A customer rolled in a pair of worn tires and asked for his money back. Nordstrom sells clothing and shoes. It had bought its Alaska stores in 1975 from Northern Commercial, a company that did sell tires. Craig Trounce, a teenage sales associate, called a tire dealer, settled on a fair value of $25, and paid the customer from the till. Nordstrom[still tells the story](https://press.nordstrom.com/news-releases/news-release-details/nordy-pod-truth-about-nordstroms-legendary-tire-story) as a picture of its service culture.


Stories like that one shaped what shoppers expect today. Demand for convenient returns rose on every measure Happy Returns tracks in 2026.


- **87% of shoppers say free returns are an important factor when shopping online** , up from 82% in 2025 ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).
- **81% check a retailer's return policy before purchasing** ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).
- **75% are less likely to shop with a retailer again after a poor returns experience** , up from 71% in 2025 ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).
- **53% have abandoned a purchase over the lack of a convenient return method** ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).
- **25% would eliminate waiting for a refund if they could remove one part of the returns process** , the most common answer ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).
- **44% of shoppers would view a retailer more favorably if it offered an AI-enabled chatbot to guide returns** ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).
- **48% of retailers believe AI agents could most improve customer service inquiries** , level with fraud detection and inventory management ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).


### How fast support answers a return request (Yuma benchmark data)


Shoppers hate waiting more than anything else. Yuma's benchmark shows how long the support side of that wait runs across 100+ merchants.


- **Median time to resolution is 2.8 hours across all channels** , and under 1.8 hours for the top quartile ([Yuma](https://yuma.ai/cx-automation-benchmark-2026) , 2026).
- **The best merchants send a first response in under 1 minute on live channels** , against an 18-minute median across all channels ([Yuma](https://yuma.ai/cx-automation-benchmark-2026) , 2026).
- **Email carries 73% of support volume** , with chat at 6% and help center, SMS, and social at 21% ([Yuma](https://yuma.ai/cx-automation-benchmark-2026) , 2026).
- **Median CSAT is 4.5 out of 5** , and 4.7 or higher for the top quartile ([Yuma](https://yuma.ai/cx-automation-benchmark-2026) , 2026).


## What returns do to your support queue


AI agents can only resolve a refund or return ticket when the merchant lets them by giving them permission to issue refunds plus connections to Shopify and the returns portal. Without both, the agent passes the ticket to a person, which is why money-related tickets get handed off more often than simple questions.


Consider a routine customer email asking to swap a jacket for a larger size. Resolving that single message requires checking policy eligibility, verifying warehouse stock, generating a return label, and creating a replacement order. Each step touches a different system. An AI agent connected to only some of them hands the ticket to a human.


Yuma's[2026 CX automation benchmark](https://yuma.ai/cx-automation-benchmark-2026) analyzed production ticket data from 100+ active Shopify and Shopify Plus merchants over a 90-day window (March 14 to June 12, 2026) to measure how these workflows perform at scale.


- **The typical merchant automates 71% of eligible tickets on its best day** , while the top-performing brand sustains 87% automation across a full quarter.
- **Money-involving tickets lag behind informational inquiries.** Product and brand questions exceed 70% best-day automation across every revenue tier. Tickets involving returns, refunds, and order edits escalate more often. The benchmark attributes the difference to setup, meaning the authority and integrations a merchant gives its AI. Top performers have automated the money-touching workflows, such as returns and order modifications, that the median merchant still escalates.
- **Higher automation leaves CSAT level.** Automation runs from under 40% to nearly 90% across the cohort while CSAT barely moves. The correlation between the two is -0.18, which the benchmark calls statistically negligible.
- **The median merchant saves a modeled 271 agent-hours per quarter** , and the top quartile saves 940 or more. The benchmark models the figure at a loaded agent cost of €25 per hour.


### Automation and CSAT by vertical


Best-day automation is nearly identical across verticals, while CSAT varies more. Apparel and fashion posts the lowest CSAT in the cohort, which the benchmark links to returns-heavy, fit-driven categories industry-wide.


- **Apparel and fashion** reaches 73% best-day automation with a CSAT of 4.3.
- **Beauty and personal care** reaches 73% with a CSAT of 4.5.
- **Electronics and tech** reaches 73% with a CSAT of 4.5.
- **Health and supplements** reaches 71% with a CSAT of 4.7.
- **Home and lifestyle** reaches 71% with a CSAT of 4.7.
- **Food and beverage** reaches 69% with a CSAT of 4.7.


### Automation by revenue tier and helpdesk


Store size and helpdesk choice move the result by only a few points.


- **Emerging brands (under $5M)** reach 73% best-day automation with a CSAT of 4.6.
- **Growth brands ($5M to $25M)** reach 70% with a CSAT of 4.5.
- **Scale brands ($25M to $100M)** reach 71% with a CSAT of 4.4.
- **Enterprise brands ($100M+)** reach 67% with a CSAT of 4.4.
- **Helpdesk choice barely moves the number.** Best-day automation is 72.7% on Zendesk, 71.6% on Re:amaze, and 71.1% on Gorgias.


The top performer in Yuma's benchmark is[The Bradery](https://yuma.ai/case-studies/the-bradery) , a Paris-based fashion flash-sale site. Every daily sale launch brings a burst of questions about deliveries, order changes and returns. The Bradery automated 87% of eligible tickets across the full quarter, with a best day of 94%.


EvryJewels, a jewelry and accessories brand, averages 80% with a 92% best day. Freebird handled 117,000 tickets in the 90-day window with 59% automated, while Cabaïa escalated 15.8% of 28,000 tickets.


What sets the top performers apart is that their AI agents carry out the action itself, such as issuing a refund or changing an order. Yuma's benchmark found that top performers automate returns and order changes, which the median merchant still hands to a person. In practice that means[automated returns and refunds](https://yuma.ai/use-cases/sup002-instantly-process-returns-and-refunds-with-zero-agent-time) ,[automated product exchanges](https://yuma.ai/use-cases/handle-product-exchanges-for-size-or-color-automatically) , and[order edits and cancellations](https://yuma.ai/use-cases/edit-or-cancel-orders-before-they-ship) that catch a mistaken purchase before the order leaves the warehouse.


## Returns KPIs worth tracking (and how to benchmark them)


A shared set of returns and support metrics gives operations, finance, and CX leaders the same baseline when they evaluate vendors or defend headcount budgets.


- **Return rate by channel.** Compare your monthly numbers against the 18% online and 15% total averages ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026) and your own historical baseline to catch sizing or manufacturing defects early.
- **Holiday return rate.** Retailers expect 19% of 2026 holiday sales back ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026). Measure your November to January rate separately from the annual figure.
- **Fraud and abuse flag rate.** Fraud accounts for 8% of returns ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026), while about 1% of shoppers are marked as risky returners ([Happy Returns and Wyllo](https://happyreturns.com/resource/fraud-report-2026) , June 2026). Monitor flagged returns by method, since mail-in carries six times the fraud rate of in-person drop-off.
- **Return fee outcomes.** Track return rate, exchange rate, and complaint volume before and after any fee change. Return rates fell after fees for 41% of the retailers that charge them, while 50% saw more complaints ([Happy Returns](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) , 2026).
- **Automation rate on return tickets.**[Yuma](https://yuma.ai/cx-automation-benchmark-2026) 's benchmark tracks all eligible tickets (71% on a typical best day and 87% sustained), so segment returns and refund tickets in your helpdesk reporting to measure how many close without human touch.
- **CSAT on automated tickets.** The median across Yuma's cohort is 4.5 out of 5, with the top quartile at 4.7 or higher. Track CSAT beside your automation rate, since the benchmark found the two move independently.
- **Time to resolution on return tickets.** The benchmark median is 2.8 hours across all channels, with the top quartile under 1.8 hours.
- **Peak-month multiplier.** Divide your busiest month's ticket volume by a normal month's. The benchmark median is 1.5x, with the busiest quartile at 2.2x or higher.

## Methodology and sources


Every statistic in this article is cited to its original publisher.


- **Happy Returns:**[Returns Happen 2026](https://happyreturns.com/returns-happen-2026) (published 2026). Fifth annual study, based on surveys of 2,006 consumers who returned at least one online purchase in the past 12 months and 375 ecommerce professionals at US retailers with $250M or more in revenue.
- **Happy Returns and Wyllo:**[The Hidden Threat in Your Returns: How to Spot, Stop, and Prevent Return Fraud](https://happyreturns.com/resource/fraud-report-2026) (published June 2026). Based on aggregated and anonymized behavioral and transactional data observed across the Wyllo consortium network between January 2025 and April 2026.
- **Yuma:**[The State of CX Automation in Ecommerce 2026](https://yuma.ai/cx-automation-benchmark-2026) (published 2026). Production benchmark analyzing 100+ active Shopify and Shopify Plus merchants over a 90-day window (March 14 to June 12, 2026), with seasonality built on 12 months of ticket history (June 2025 to May 2026).
- **Retail history:**[Britannica](https://www.britannica.com/biography/Montgomery-Ward) on Montgomery Ward's 1875 money-back guarantee, the[Associated Press](https://komonews.com/news/business/ll-bean-dropping-its-unlimited-returns-policy-02-09-2018-163629377) on L.L.Bean's 2018 return policy change (February 9, 2018), and[Nordstrom](https://press.nordstrom.com/news-releases/news-release-details/nordy-pod-truth-about-nordstroms-legendary-tire-story) and[Alaska Airlines](https://news.alaskaair.com/alaska-airlines/nordstrom-tire-story/) on the Fairbanks tire return.
